CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
Yesterday's high temperatures once again reached into the mid 60s across most areas, as the 00Z DTX sounding checked in with a 925 mb temp of 11 C. Temperatures should be even warmer today (65 to 70 degrees) as 925 mb temps are advertised to reach near 13 C. Thus, there is an excellent chance Flint ties or breaks its daily record high for Nov 21. A weaker pressure gradient over eastern areas will allow surface flow backed a bit more out of the south-southeast to exert some cooler marine influence and thus result in the lower values. An upper-level wave and cold pool sinking south into Montana today will team up with a strong PV anomaly descending south out of the Arctic Circle and sliding south along the Manitoba/Ontario border on Sunday. This will lead to much colder temperatures next week. One more warm day is expected on Sunday, with temperatures likely rising back into the low to mid 60s as a cold front and rain showers arrive late in the day into early Sunday evening. With the main low and height falls tracking north of Lower Michigan, indications are that the line of showers along the frontal boundary will be in a weakening state as it crosses Southeast Michigan, and QPF amounts will likely be under a tenth of an inch, with some locations struggling to even measure. Aggressive drying arrives by midnight as 700 mb dewpoint depressions increase to 30 C by Monday morning. Nonetheless, a strong upper- level wave will swing through northern Lower Michigan Monday evening and send 850 mb temps into the -9 to -12 C range. There is an increasing chance (supported by the Euro model) that the northern Thumb region will see light accumulating snow, as there is even synoptic support from the narrow, short-lived forcing along the Arctic boundary tracking through Monday evening. A 700 mb cold pool (-20C) will track across Lake Huron Monday night, with warming and an upper-level ridge quickly building in on Tuesday, putting an end to any potential lake-effect activity. The low-level air mass will remain chilly as 850 mb temps are progged to hold in the negative mid single digits, resulting in maxes holding in the low to mid 40s for the midweek period. && .MARINE... High pressure extending from the Great Lakes to east coast will provide light winds and mostly clear skies to start the weekend. Ridge of high pressure is also present in the upper levels across the eastern conus while a deep trough exits across the western conus. This all leads to a period of southerly flow and a warm stable airmass over the region at least to start the weekend. As the trough pushes eastward, a surface low will lift northeast through the Midwest setting up a cold front that will pass through the region Sunday evening into the overnight. This will open the door for stronger northwesterly flow and cold air advection pushing across the lakes. At this point the winds look to stay at or below 30 knots, but there will be potential for at least Small Craft Advisories Sunday night into the new week with the increasing winds and building wave heights. && .CLIMATE... Record high max temperatures for November 21st: Detroit: 67 Degrees (Set in 1913) Flint: 66 Degrees (Set in 1931) Saginaw: 69 Degrees (Set in 1913) Record high max temperatures for November 22nd: Detroit: 69 Degrees (Set in 1913) Flint: 65 Degrees (Set in 1934) Saginaw: 66 Degrees (Set in 1913) && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1142 PM EST Fri Nov 20 2026 AVIATION... South flow over Lake Erie is already driving a lake induced fog plume along the northern shores of the lake. Available surface observations and RAP 950mb winds suggest some southeasterly component to the winds over western Lake Erie Fri evening. This has likely led to some added boundary layer moisture into metro Detroit, supportive of hi res model solutions which indicate an expanding region of fog developing during the early morning hours Saturday. For the reason, fog has been expanding in the metro TAFs with a period of LIFR conditions introduced in the 10 to 13Z time frame. A more southerly component to the sfc winds farther north and recent hi res guidance supports leaving the mention of fog out of the PTK, FNT and MBS TAFs. values.   

An upper-level wave and cold pool sinking south into Montana today 
will team up with a strong PV anomaly descending south out of the

Sunday. This will lead to much colder temperatures next week. One
